title: Progress on the mechanism of pathological injury secondary to venous stroke and their therapeutic strategies: A narrative review
one_line_summary: This review summarizes secondary brain injury pathomechanisms following cerebral venous thrombosis—including blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, ER stress, and excitotoxicity—along with potential targeted therapeutic strategies.
key_pearls: The incidence of **cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT)** ranges from **1.3–1.6 cases per 100,000 population**, carrying a case fatality rate up to **34.2%** in severe cases.

Early **blood–brain barrier (BBB)** disruption post-CVT is driven by pericyte-derived **MMP-9** activation, **VEGF**-mediated **claudin-5** destruction, **JAK2V617F** thromboinflammation, and **neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)** accumulation.
Glymphatic system dysfunction and **NETs**-mediated damage to meningeal lymphatic drainage impair cerebrospinal fluid clearance, worsening intracranial hypertension and cerebral edema.

Post-CVT neuroinflammation involves rapid invasion of **neutrophils** and **CD4+ T cells**, along with an **M1 microglial** shift releasing **IL-1β**, **IL-18**, and **TNF-α** via **cGAS-STING** and **HMGB1-RAGE** pathways.
Mitochondrial **ROS** and peroxynitrite surge on **days 1–2** post-CVT, driving nitrative stress (marked by **3-nitrotyrosine**) and activating the **TXNIP/NLRP3** inflammasome pathway.
Endoplasmic reticulum stress sensors (**p-IRE1α**, **p-PERK**) and glutamate-induced **excitotoxicity** co-mediate neuronal apoptosis and neurovascular breakdown.

sections.heading: Introduction and Epidemiology of Venous Stroke
sections.content:
- Cerebral venous thrombosis (**CVT**), or venous stroke, is a distinct stroke subtype predominantly affecting young adults and children.
- Reported incidence ranges from **1.3–1.6 cases per 100,000 population** in developed countries, with higher rates observed in Asian populations.
- Severe **CVT** causes cerebral venous infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, raised intracranial pressure (**ICP**), and neurovascular endothelial damage.
- Case fatality in severe **CVT** reaches up to **34.2%**, and **20% to 40%** of survivors suffer long-term neurological deficits including seizures, psychiatric injury, and altered consciousness.
- Mainstream acute care is currently limited to anticoagulation, thrombolysis, and endovascular therapy, creating an unmet need for neuroprotective interventions targeting secondary injury.
section_pearls: Case fatality in severe CVT reaches **34.2%**, with **20–40%** left with permanent neurological deficits.

sections.heading: Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption, Impaired Lymphatic Drainage, and Brain Edema
sections.content:
- Obstruction of venous return increases capillary hydrostatic pressure, lowering local perfusion and causing focal ischemia/hypoxia that triggers vasogenic and cytotoxic cerebral edema.
- Microvascular basilemma collagen IV breakdown begins within **3 hours** post-**CVT**, accompanied by serum leakage of tight junction proteins (**ZO-1**, **claudin-5**).
- Pericyte-derived **MMP-9** degrades basement membrane proteins; circulating **MMP-9** serves as a biomarker for parenchymal brain lesions and persistent venous occlusion.
- Neuronal **VEGF** expression increases under hypoxic conditions, downregulating **claudin-5** and promoting vascular permeability.
- **JAK2V617F** gene mutations accelerate platelet/neutrophil adhesion, driving thromboinflammation and **BBB** breakdown.
- **NETs** accumulate in plasma, thrombi, and brain parenchyma, converting endothelia to a procoagulant phenotype and impairing meningeal lymphatic drainage.
- Astrocyte **AQP4** dysregulation and perivascular space enlargement disrupt glymphatic waste clearance, exacerbating **ICP** and hydrocephalus.
section_pearls: Pericyte-derived **MMP-9** and **VEGF**-mediated **claudin-5** degradation drive early BBB hyperpermeability post-CVT.
Accumulation of **NETs** creates a vicious circle of BBB breakdown and meningeal lymphatic obstruction.

sections.heading: Immunoinflammatory Cascade
sections.content:
- Post-**CVT** inflammation initiates within minutes and persists for **7–14 days**, characterized by peripheral leukocyte recruitment and local microglial activation.
- **Neutrophils** invade cerebral parenchyma within **1–2 days**, releasing lysozymes, cytokines, and **NETs** that stimulate microglial dsDNA receptors.
- Resident **microglia** proliferate and adopt an amoeboid M1 proinflammatory phenotype colocalized with **IL-1β** at **1–3 days**, transitioning toward a branching M2 reparative phenotype by **day 7**.
- Infiltrating **CD4+ T cells** and double-negative **T cells** (**CD3+ CD4- CD8-**) promote microglial neuroinflammation, while **CD8+ T cells** secrete neurotoxic proteases.
- Transcriptomic analyses confirm **significant** upregulation of inflammatory mediators (**IL-1β**, **Tlr4**, **Itgam**, **Tlr2**, **CCl-2**) and enriched pathways (**NF-κB**, **NLR**, **TLR**, complement/coagulation cascades, **cGAS-STING**, and **HMGB1-RAGE** axes).
section_pearls: Microglial M1 proinflammatory activation peaks at **3 days** post-CVT and shifts toward an M2 phenotype by **day 7**.
Activation of the **cGAS-STING** and **HMGB1-RAGE** pathways drives post-CVT neuroinflammation.

sections.heading: Oxidative and Nitrative Stress
sections.content:
- Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (**ROS**) and peroxynitrite surge uncontrollably on **days 1–2** post-**CVT** in forebrain neurons.
- Lipid peroxidation markers (**malondialdehyde**) increase while endogenous antioxidants (**Mn-SOD**, **GPx**) are markedly depleted.
- Protein tyrosine nitration marker **3-nitrotyrosine** increases **significantly** in cortical neurons and microglia.
- **ROS** and peroxynitrite upregulate **TXNIP**, which binds thioredoxin (**TRX**) to inhibit its antioxidant function and directly activates the **NLRP3** inflammasome.
- Transcriptomic data show post-**CVT** downregulation of hemoglobin genes **Hba** and **Hbb**, signaling reduced neuronal oxygen-binding capacity exacerbated by oxidative stress.
section_pearls: Peroxynitrite and **ROS** upregulate **TXNIP**, coupling nitrative stress directly to **NLRP3** inflammasome activation.

sections.heading: Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Excitotoxicity
sections.content:
- Unfolded protein response (**UPR**) transmembrane sensors **p-IRE1α** and **p-PERK** are rapidly phosphorylated in neurons post-**CVT**.
- Activation of **p-IRE1α** and **p-PERK** induces **TXNIP**, **CHOP**, and **caspase-12**, correlating directly with early neurobehavioral deficits and infarct volume.
- **ER** stress directly contributes to **MMP-9** activation and subsequent **BBB** structural breakdown.
- Cortical **glutamate** levels peak on **days 1–2** post-**CVT**, accompanied by compensatory downregulation of **NMDA** receptor subunits (**NR1**, **NR2A**, **NR2B**).
- Glutamate-induced excitotoxicity impairs **ER** intracellular *Ca2+* homeostasis, creating a damaging feedback loop between **ER** stress and excitotoxic neuronal death.
section_pearls: Glutamate excitotoxicity and **ER** stress (**p-IRE1α**/**p-PERK**) reinforce each other to drive early neuronal apoptosis.

sections.heading: Therapeutic Strategies Targeting Secondary Pathology
sections.content:
- Pharmacological free radical scavenging using **edaravone** or **edaravone dexborneol** and therapeutic **hypothermia** show neuroprotective potential adapted from arterial stroke paradigms.
- Combined endovascular therapy (**thrombectomy**, **thrombolysis**), therapeutic **hypothermia**, and **decompressive craniectomy** improve functional outcomes in malignant **CVT** with impending herniation.
- Mechanical thrombectomy effectively lowers parenchymal **glutamate** concentrations and elevated **ICP** monitored via cerebral microdialysis.
- Short-term **steroid** administration combined with systemic **anticoagulation** represents a promising adjunctive therapy for acute/subacute severe **CVT**, pending confirmation by randomized controlled trials.
section_pearls: Mechanical thrombectomy reduces local parenchymal **glutamate** levels and **ICP** in severe CVT.
Short-term **steroids** combined with **anticoagulants** show early promise as adjunctive therapy in severe CVT.

strengths_limitations:
- *Strengths*: Synthesizes recent transcriptomic data and molecular pathomechanisms of secondary brain injury post-CVT; clearly outlines multi-pathway therapeutic targets.
- *Limitations*: Relying on narrative design without systematic search methodology; limited by scarce longitudinal clinical data and difficulty establishing stable CVT animal models.
